title: Empirical Evaluation of a Generate–Validate–Repair Loop for Intent→Network Configuration Using a Deterministic Reachability Validator
abstract: We evaluate whether adding a deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair (a generator–validator–repair, GVR, loop) around a single LLM (gpt-5-mini) increases the rate of correct, safely executable network configurations synthesized from natural-language intents versus plain LLM generation. In a fully preregistered paired design (cns-m2026-01) we processed 300 intents (600 episodes, shared-initial baseline semantics). Baseline succeeded in 299/300 tasks (99.67%); guarded (validator ± one repair) succeeded in 300/300 (100%). Paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01]. The preregistered target (10 percentage-point absolute improvement) is not supported because the baseline was near ceiling. We release full execution and scoring artifacts (paths and SHA-256 hashes archived) and discuss operational interpretation, failure modes, and when GVR loops are likely to be consequential.

sections.introduction: LLMs are being proposed for intent-driven NetOps (intent→configuration) but operational deployment requires guarantees that generated device configurations are correct and do not cause unintended reachability or safety changes. Architectures that interpose validators and repair steps around a generator are widely advocated, yet empirical, preregistered measurements of their marginal operational benefit are scarce. We ask: Does inserting a deterministic reachability validator and a single automated repair step around an LLM increase the proportion of intents that yield execution-validated, safely executable configurations compared with plain LLM generation? We ran a preregistered paired experiment (cns-m2026-01) comparing (a) a shared-initial LLM candidate used as the baseline and (b) the same candidate passed to a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) with at most one automated repair if the validator rejected it. Contributions: (1) a fully preregistered, artifact-backed paired study (N=300); (2) complete auditable artifacts (model calls, provider traces, validator traces, per-episode scoring) with recorded SHA-256 hashes; (3) empirical evidence and operational guidance showing that when baseline generator accuracy is near ceiling a single-step GVR gate yields negligible measurable improvement.
sections.related_work: Work motivating verifier-assisted NetOps includes NetConfEval (intent→config evaluation), practical intent-validation pipelines for network automation, and closed-loop proposer/verifier architectures that separate proposal from verification. Our contribution is an artifact-grounded, preregistered, paired measurement that quantifies the marginal benefit of a single verification+repair gate on a controlled intent distribution. Representative leads (archival references in cited_record_ids) informed design and validator selection.
sections.methodology: Preregistration: Study preregistered as cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA-256: 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). Design: paired binary outcome per intent (baseline vs guarded), unit = intent, N=300. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline. Task generation and contamination: 300 intent→configuration tasks were deterministically generated; contamination filters and selection RNG seeds are archived (execution/task_manifest.jsonl; SHA-256 = 91564bb69ac692e2fbd6321708863d13938309b5433ef1b211541ba5426df990). Shared-initial baseline semantics (preregistered): each intent used a single shared initial generator call; guarded re-used the identical shared candidate and then invoked deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and, if needed, at most one automated repair call. This design isolates validator/repair effect on identical generator proposals. Implementation: model declared as gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820), provider = openai_responses. Execution budget: planned max model calls = 600; observed model_calls_used = 301 (execution manifest). Validator and scoring: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applied closed-world reachability and intent-constraint checks; per-episode scoring files and validator traces are archived (examples in analysis/artifacts and execution/scoring/). Analysis: preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 computed exact McNemar two-sided p and bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed=1729). All provider-call traces, responses, scoring JSON, and hashes are archived (execution/execution_manifest.json).
sections.results: Primary confirmatory outcome (artifact: analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv; SHA-256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55): complete_pair_count = 300. Baseline successes = 299/300 (99.67%); guarded successes = 300/300 (100.0%). Contingency counts: n11 = 299, n10 = 1 (guarded=1, baseline=0), n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Paired difference = 0.00333. Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.01] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). Provider-call accounting (execution manifest) shows model_calls_used = 301, shared_initial_generation = 300, repair calls = 1. The lone repair call and the single discordant pair are archived: provider repair trace at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (SHA-256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba), and the per-episode responses/validator traces for that episode are archived at execution/responses/task-000117-baseline.txt (SHA-256 = 2422520c3cbfd26a45a7232100cdf5d4fb9ccc5e00c01f8ca4854499d13e7d70) and execution/responses/task-000117-guarded.txt (SHA-256 = 5f1dc27b7325694bfbd67caa42c06db285fdfc825d2a41d2039d9e28628b0e7d). Missingness/technical failures: none (failed_episode_count = 0). Sensitivity arithmetic: preregistered target was a 10 percentage-point absolute increase (Δ=0.10). Detecting Δ=0.10 in a paired design with N=300 requires ≥30 one-sided discordant pairs; observed discordant-pair sum = 1, so the experiment could not detect the preregistered target because baseline was near ceiling.
sections.discussion: Interpretation: the shared-initial LLM generator produced near-ceiling correct configurations on this deterministic task set, leaving negligible room for a single-step GVR gate to improve aggregate success. The GVR loop did correct one isolated generator mistake (the single repair archived at execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json; SHA-256 above), but this produced only a +0.33 percentage-point absolute change. Operational implication: validator+repair gates can fix individual generator errors, but measurable benefit requires (a) a higher baseline error rate (e.g., human-authored or adversarial intents), (b) more permissive repair budgeting (multi-iteration repair), or (c) more challenging task distributions. Preregistered hypothesis H2 ("Among residual failures after the GVR loop, a plurality are attributable to ambiguous or underspecified natural-language intents") is untestable here because there were zero residual failures after the guarded pipeline (guarded success count = 300). Consequently H2 cannot be evaluated from these artifacts; we therefore report it as preregistered but unassessable given the observed data. For completeness: the single discordant pair (baseline failed, guarded succeeded) is episode task-000117; the baseline and guarded per-episode responses and the guard repair trace are archived (paths and SHA-256 values cited above) and show the repair call corrected a validator-detected safety ordering omission. Threats to validity: internal—shared-initial semantics intentionally isolate validator effect but do not measure candidate regeneration strategies; construct—the validator operationalizes safety as absence of unintended reachability changes in the emulator (pragmatic but partial); external—deterministic synthetic tasks limit generality to production human-authored intent distributions; model scope—single-model (gpt-5-mini) evaluation limits cross-model generality. All artifacts supporting these statements are archived and hashed in the execution manifest.
sections.conclusion: In this fully preregistered paired experiment (N=300) a single-step deterministic reachability validator plus at most one automated repair produced one additional success over a high-performing baseline generator (299→300). Because baseline accuracy was near ceiling the preregistered target improvement (10 percentage points) is not supported. We release complete artifacts (provider traces, responses, validator traces, scoring JSON, analysis artifacts and hashes) so future work can explore harder task distributions, multi-iteration repair policies, alternative generator/regeneration strategies, or multi-model comparisons to characterize when GVR loops yield operationally meaningful gains.

disclosure_statement:
Mandatory Disclosure Statement — autonomous run provenance and artifacts

This paper was produced by an autonomous post-lock research run governed by the Master Prompt v1 and preregistration cns-m2026-01 (preregistration SHA-256 = 0726a6c02c1ed6fc379927f4bb0696330f0b00484f15caee5cf4ebc072316bf7). Initial master prompt immutable reference: provenance/master_prompt.txt (SHA-256 = 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role: Research Director supplied the broad topic constraint (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and participated in pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsal only; after the autonomy lock all literature discovery, preregistration, experiment design, execution, analysis, manuscript drafting, autonomous peer-review, and revisions were performed autonomously by the system. No human manually edited technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock.

Models and configuration: declared model = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json; SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). Provider: openai_responses (provider traces archived). Orchestration and adapter: hosted_netops_gvr_v1 implementing shared-initial baseline semantics and the guarded pipeline that calls deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and, when needed per preregistered policy, at most one automated repair. Full model-call logs, provider traces, response files, validator traces, per-episode scoring JSON, and all analysis artifacts are archived and hashed in the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json). Key artifact references used in the manuscript: execution/execution_manifest.json (full manifest and hashes); analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv (SHA-256 = 3421adb52d5791a979397368165fc2062e6b9a4a771ce49c0bcac80b02215d55); analysis/condition_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 55eacb88c64f29dc9c5ce1ca7079eca9b4a94b5d3a2970dae019a81a1decf73b); execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json (the single observed repair call; SHA-256 = 4deb410d5736ab332cd5caaf00b16051e5b0aef2276255c0770098f63cb523ba); execution/responses/task-000117-baseline.txt (SHA-256 = 2422520c3cbfd26a45a7232100cdf5d4fb9ccc5e00c01f8ca4854499d13e7d70) and execution/responses/task-000117-guarded.txt (SHA-256 = 5f1dc27b7325694bfbd67caa42c06db285fdfc825d2a41d2039d9e28628b0e7d). The execution manifest records model_calls_used = 301 (shared_initial_generation = 300; repair calls = 1) and the complete hash manifest of all artifacts (execution/execution_manifest.json).

Preregistration, selection, and analysis: The experiment design, inclusion/exclusion rules, contamination and selection procedures, stopping and retry policies, and the primary analysis plan (paired binary McNemar-style test; bootstrap CI) were preregistered and not changed after observing outcomes (see preregistration cns-m2026-01 archived and SHA-256 above). Shared-initial semantics were preregistered to isolate the effect of the validator and repair on identical generator proposals; this means we measured the marginal effect of verification/repair on the same candidate rather than the effect of independently re-generating alternative candidates under guarded prompts. The execution followed the preregistered analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1); results and analysis artifacts are archived (analysis/*; SHA-256 values provided). The confirmatory primary test yielded paired counts n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; paired difference = 0.00333; exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.01].

Autonomy boundary and pre-lock work: The Research Director and human collaborators performed pre-lock infrastructure development and rehearsal; those pre-lock runs were not used as empirical evidence for the final study. After the autonomy lock the system autonomously executed literature discovery, gap selection, preregistration, experiment execution, artifact archiving, analysis, autonomous peer review, and manuscript revisions. No human manually rewrote technical claims after the lock.

Technical restarts and failures: The run completed without unrecoverable technical failures; failed_episode_count = 0. Retry policy (preregistered) allowed up to two automated retries for transient provider or container start-up errors; such retries were logged in execution/execution_log.jsonl. The single automated repair occurred under the preregistered repair budget and is archived (execution/provider_calls/task-000117-guarded-repair.json; SHA-256 above). All provider calls and cached call artifacts are archived under execution/call_cache/ with listed SHA-256 hashes. The deterministic_reconciliation artifact affirms internal accounting consistency (analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json; archived).
limitations: Ceiling effect: baseline success = 299/300 limits detectable improvement; detecting the preregistered 10% absolute increase would require ≥30 one-sided discordant pairs, but observed discordant-pair sum = 1.
Task scope: tasks were deterministically generated synthetic intent→configuration examples; external validity to human-authored, adversarial, or production intent distributions is limited.
Model scope: single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) — results do not generalize automatically to other models or fine-tuned variants.
Validator construct: safety was operationalized as absence of unintended reachability changes in an emulated environment — a pragmatic but partial proxy for operational NetOps safety.
Repair budget: only one automated repair attempt per task was allowed (preregistered); multi-iteration repair strategies were not explored in this confirmatory run.
